neighbours.label: the 1950s: a number from 1950 to 1959 in a text set in the 1950s (Eisenhower, early television, rock and roll, the polio vaccine, Sputnik), whether it is a year or a count; the same 195x count in a modern or other-era text, and other decades' years in the same kind of text, stay low
fire: Elvis had just appeared on Ed Sullivan. The drive-in sold 1953 tickets that night.
Ike was in the White House and the suburbs were booming. The new subdivision had 1957 houses.
Families gathered around their first TV sets. The station got 1955 letters from viewers.
Rock and roll was new and teenagers loved it. The record shop sold 1958 copies in a week.
Senator McCarthy was hunting communists, and by 1954 his hearings were on television.
The polio vaccine was being tested in schools, and in 1955 the results were announced.
Sputnik had just alarmed the country, and in 1958 NASA was founded.
Hula hoops were the latest craze, and in 1958 millions of them were sold.
quiet: Influencers had just posted about it online. The drive-in sold 1953 tickets that night.
Lincoln was in the White House and the railroads were booming. The new town had 1957 houses.
Families gathered around their new smartphones. The station got 1955 emails from viewers.
Streaming had replaced albums and teenagers loved it. The record shop sold 1958 vinyl copies in a week.
Senator Douglas was debating Lincoln, and by 1858 their debates were in every newspaper.
The smallpox vaccine was being tested in villages, and in 1796 the results were announced.
The Moon landing had just thrilled the country, and in 1970 the EPA was founded.
Pet rocks were the latest craze, and in 1975 millions of them were sold.

notes: Second round on my own held label (round 1: #392, 'the 1950s (in digits)'). Reason, written before this test: a context year atlas (every year 1700-2029 read as a year, as a count, and as a count after a no-digit cue sentence about the matching era, an era 50 or 100 years away, or a modern setting; discovery only) found this pole's 195x readings strongly gated by context: inside 1950-59 it read 0.23 as a bare year in 'She was born in Y.', 0.05 as a plain count, 0.03 as a count in a modern cue, but 0.72 as a count after a 1950s cue (0.13 with a cue 50 years off, 0.06 with one 100 years off). Across the late decade units (layers 21-27, n=80) the same pattern holds on average: count 0.09, matched era 0.22, era 50 years off 0.13, era 100 years off 0.09. This round tests the context-gated label on fresh cues; no cue sentence of the atlas is reused. Scoring runs on a Modal L40S (bfloat16; PARITY OK on Modal).
